events.description: Thornton memo to Brzezinski offering three hypotheses on Soviet role in Kabul leadership changes.
Dismissal of military in cabinet, retirement of Taraki, and Amin's announcement of end of one-man leadership.
Soviets made a fuss over Taraki in Moscow the week before the memo.
Thornton memo to Brzezinski assessing Soviet role in Afghan leadership change, offering three hypotheses.
Soviets received Taraki in Moscow with great fanfare the week before the memo.
Over the weekend: military dismissed from cabinet, Taraki retired, and Amin announced the end of one-man leadership.

relationships.detail: Amin took over after Taraki was dropped/retired.
relationships.quote: after the dropping of Taraki, the Soviets stepped in, called his bluff

relationships.detail: Soviets honored Taraki in Moscow the week before.
relationships.quote: The Soviets made quite a fuss over Taraki last week in Moscow

relationships.detail: Hypothesis that Amin acted in defiance of the Soviets.
relationships.quote: Amin is doing the whole thing in defiance of the Soviets

relationships.detail: Amin ousted the military men from the cabinet.
relationships.quote: ouster of the military men may denote foreknowledge, but not necessarily complicity

relationships.detail: Thornton writes information memo to Brzezinski.
Memo issued on National Security Council letterhead.
The Soviets made a fuss over Taraki the previous week in Moscow.
relationships.quote: The Soviets made quite a fuss over Taraki last week in Moscow

relationships.detail: Taraki was in Moscow the week before the memo.
relationships.quote: The Soviets made quite a fuss over Taraki last week in Moscow

relationships.detail: Amin's moves forced Taraki's retirement; may be a slap at Taraki.
relationships.quote: nothing more than a gratuitous slap at Taraki

relationships.detail: Under hypothesis 2, Amin acts in defiance of the Soviets, presenting a fait accompli.
relationships.quote: Amin is doing the whole thing in defiance of the Soviets, facing them with a fait accompli.

relationships.detail: Under hypothesis 3, Soviets called Amin's bluff and force collective leadership on him.
relationships.quote: the Soviets stepped in, called his bluff, and are now forcing him to accept a collective leadership

relationships.detail: Soviets would have no reason to do in the military faction.
relationships.quote: the Soviets would not seem to have any reason to do in the military faction

relationships.detail: Amin announced the end of one-man leadership of the government in Kabul.
relationships.quote: Amin's announcement of the end of one-man leadership
a more acceptable government installed in Kabul

key_claims: US analysts did not know what the Soviets were doing in Afghanistan.
Three hypotheses: Soviet stage-management, Amin acting in defiance, or Soviets forcing collective leadership after Taraki's fall.
Thornton judged Soviet stage-management least likely and favored Amin acting in defiance.
The Soviets are seen as unable to come out winners and closer to their moment of truth.
The memo recommends making the Soviets appear to have a hand in Amin's operation.
